newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary stock market ends lower, futures plunge.
newsitem.headline: Hungary stock market ends lower, futures plunge.

text.p: Share prices fell on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Wednesday and the futures market also plunged as Hungarian stocks triggered little interest on the SEAQ in London, traders said.
"There were sellers (in Hungarian stocks) in London, whereas I didn't see buyers at all," said Istvan Simon of Concorde Securities.
The BUX index closed at 5,451.88 points, down 78.68.
BUX futures fell for all maturities by between 122.50 and 152.50 points. The March BUX fell below today's spot index to close at 5,445.5 points, down 131.50.
Leading Hungarian stocks trade on London's SEAQ, including chemicals TVK and Borsodchem, oil company MOL and OTP Bank .

These four stocks were among the Budapest bourse's leading losers. OTP fell 105 forints to close at 3,745; TVK lost 60 forints to finish at 2,225; Borsodchem fell 150 forints to 6,430, while MOL fell 40 forints to 3,105.

Elsewhere on the market, retailer Fotex bucked the trend and closed one forint higher at 156. The movement was attributed to German investors buying the paper in connection with a private bond issue by the company.
Traders, however, turned more optimistic following today's speech by U.S. Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan.

"Today's trend could be attributed to the fact that everybody was waiting for Greenspan's speech which turned out to be surprisingly positive," Simon said. "This may mean the end of the current vacuum at least in the U.S. and this may spread over to here."
Nevertheless, traders said that the market remained hungry for news to trade on.
